sections.tabSummary: Why capacity, not top speed, defines this centrifuge
body: Learn why capacity, not top speed, defines the Kubota Model 8730.

Blood bank and clinical laboratory work rarely needs the 15,000-22,000 rpm range that Kubota's research centrifuges reach, it needs enough capacity to process real batches of blood bags and large bottles at a controlled temperature, reliably, run after run. Model 8730 is built around exactly that priority: a maximum capacity of 4,000 mL, blood bag compatibility built directly into the rotor design, and a temperature range wide enough to protect clinical samples throughout.

The rotor set reflects the same focus. 1 high capacity swinging bucket rotor handles the largest batches, and 2 multi-purpose swinging bucket rotors cover the routine tube and bottle work that fills the rest of a clinical lab's day.

sections.title: Twelve Bags, One Spin
sections.tabSummary: Why batch capacity defines this centrifuge entirely
body: Learn why batch capacity defines the Kubota Model 9945 entirely.

A blood bank doesn't process one bag at a time, it processes donations in batches, and every centrifuge cycle that handles fewer bags means more cycles, more time, and more staff hours spent loading and unloading. Model 9945 is built specifically to remove that bottleneck: 12 blood bags in a single run, on a rotor purpose-built for the 200 mL to 500 mL bag sizes standard blood collection actually uses.
There's no rotor decision to make here, no swapping between tube and plate configurations. One dedicated rotor, one job, done at the batch size a real blood bank actually needs.

sections.title: More Capacity, More Rotor Choice
sections.tabSummary: Why Model 9925 outpaces both related models
body: Learn why Model 9925 outpaces both Model 8730 and Model 9945 on capacity and speed.

Model 8730 tops out at 4,000 mL and 4,150 xg. Model 9945 is faster on RCF at 5,240 xg but limited to blood bags exclusively, with 12-bag capacity but a single rotor. Model 9925 combines the flexibility of Model 8730's mixed sample range with meaningfully higher performance across the board: 6,000 mL capacity, 7,000 rpm, and 11,290 xg, the highest numbers in Kubota's blood and clinical processing category.

The rotor set backs that up. 4 dedicated blood bags/high capacity swinging bucket rotors, 1 general swinging bucket rotor, and 1 angle rotor give a lab genuine choice between blood-bag-specific processing and standard tube or bottle work, on the same unit.
